title: One person on both sides shows one Labor, Parts row
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have an active staff member at the test location with the "Sales Representative" switch on: sales rep A.
  • Use a customer with no Sales Representative assigned.
  • Make sure the test location's Shop Supplies Charge is 0% and nothing else is invoiced at the test location today.
  • Have a first work order for that customer with one labor line of 2.00 hours at $100.00 an hour and one part sold at $50.00.
  • Have a second work order for that customer with one part sold at $50.00 and no labor.
  • On both work orders set "Sales Representative - Labor" and "Sales Representative - Parts" to sales rep A, and invoice both today.
  • Open Reports > Sales By Representative in a desktop browser at least 1024 pixels wide, with the date range set to today and the Sales Type column turned on.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The first work order's invoice is one row, Sales Type "Labor, Parts".
  • It holds the sum of both sides: Labor Invoiced $200.00 and Parts Invoiced $50.00.
  • It counts once.
  • The second work order's invoice is one row, Sales Type "Labor, Parts", with Parts Invoiced $50.00.
  • Its Labor Delta reads 0.0 (not a dash), because the invoice has no labor.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative)

  • S5-R10: “When one person, or Unassigned, holds both the Labor and the Parts side of a work order and the Sales Type filter includes both, the two show as one row whose Sales Type reads "Labor, Parts" and whose figures are the sum of both sides.”
  • S5-R13: “A representative counts an invoice once, even when they have two rows for it. When two people split an invoice, each counts it once, so the representatives' invoice counts can add up to more than the shop's.”
  • S5-R15: “On a Labor row the parts columns show a dash, and on a Parts row the labor, hours and Shop Supplies columns show a dash, not $0.00. $0.00 is shown only for a real zero. A row that holds both sides, one person on both, keeps the report's rule that an invoice with no labor shows Labor Delta 0.0.”

From: Chris Ward's answers to the Splitting Sales Representatives question sheet (answers 1 to 38, 19 Oct 2026; answers 39 and 40, 21 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 24: “24. (a) as the feature spec: a dash on screen and in the PDF, an empty cell in the CSV. The 0.0 rule still applies to an invoice with one person on both sides.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
